title: fix(lint): field-no-consumers reads a field permission's row condition (`when`) as a read of the fields it names
body:
Fixes #32282

domain:spec#2 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcSbLCxEmyHf9upz3pz
Branch: `claude/issue-32282-field-permission-when-credit`

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`field-no-consumers` 现在把字段权限的行条件 `when`(`permissions[].fields["OBJECT.FIELD"].when`)里点到的字段算作「有人读」,不再把只被这种条件读到的字段报成「没人用」。
- 为什么改:`when` 是写入闸门在每次更新前对存量行求值的 CEL 条件(如 `status in [...]` 锁字段),它确实读 `status`;此前规则只认 RLS 的 `using` / `check`,对 `when` 误报。
- 风险与回滚:只影响一条 warning 级 lint 规则的判定,不改运行时与 spec;回滚即 revert 本 PR。被授权的目标字段本身仍不算读取,仍会被报。
- 先看:`packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.ts` 的 `isFieldPermissionConditionSite` 与 `fieldPermissionObjectOf`(以及 `walk` 里用它们取对象上下文的那一行);其次同目录测试文件新增的 `[#32282]` 块。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/validate-field-consumers.test.ts`,预期 186 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.ts`:

- `isFieldPermissionConditionSite(root, segments)` names the site `permissions[].fields["OBJECT.FIELD"].when` (array or name-keyed permission set map alike). `bucketFor` buckets it as `behaviour`, beside the RLS predicate. The two key names are typed against the spec: `'fields' satisfies keyof PermissionSet` and `'when' satisfies keyof FieldPermission`.
- `fieldPermissionObjectOf` gives the entry's subtree its object: the head of the `"OBJECT.FIELD"` key before the first `.`, the reading `PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions` and `validate-rls-predicate-enforceability` both make. A permission set names no object of its own, so before this the condition's identifiers reached the walk with no object at all.
- `when` was already an expression key, so every bare identifier in it is a candidate, as in an RLS `using`.
- Only the condition is credited. The entry key (the field the permission grants on) is never read as a reference, so a field named only as a grant target is still reported. An unqualified key (no `OBJECT.` head) gives no object, so its condition credits nothing; the runtime applies such an entry nowhere.
- Module docblock: the behaviour and carrier lists and the RLS paragraph now name the field permission's condition.

`.changeset/32282-field-permission-when-credit.md`: `@objectstack/lint` patch.

The card's mechanism, measured on `origin/main` (`3452dec2`): the issue says the condition was bucketed as a carrier. On the spec's own shape it was not recorded at all. The walk carried no object into `fields["inv.region"]`, so `status` in the condition resolved to no object and was counted unresolved. The field got verdict `inert`. Either way it was reported, and the fix covers both: the site is `behaviour` and it has an object.

## Tests

New `describe('[#32282] …')` block in `packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.test.ts`, 9 cases:

- the fixture permission set passes `PermissionSetSchema.safeParse` (`when` included);
- baseline: with no condition, `inv.status` is reported;
- a field read only by a `when` is not reported;
- a field named only as the grant target (`inv.region`) still is;
- every field a compound condition names is read (`status`, `owner`);
- a name-keyed permission set map reads the same way;
- a condition that names its own grant target reads it;
- a condition credits only the object its key names (`other.status` stays reported);
- an unqualified key credits nothing.

With the site bucketed as a carrier again, `status` reads `carrier-only`. Restore: blob after restore == HEAD (`494e360b88a6`), `git diff HEAD` empty. ## Acceptance notes

- **Other conditions under `permissions` (measured, PM's question).** `PermissionSetSchema` holds two row conditions: `rowLevelSecurity[].using` / `.check`, credited already, and `fields[...].when`, credited here. `ObjectPermissionSchema` is booleans and scope enums. `tabPermissions` is an enum map, `systemPermissions` a string list. `adminScope.businessUnit` names a business unit. `protection` is prose. None of them names a field in a condition.
- **Outside `permissions`, same class, not widened.** An object's `membershipKeys.KEY.filter` is CEL over the roster object's own columns ("e.g. active == true"). `filter` is not an expression key, so a bare identifier there is not credited. Probe at `3452dec2`: a roster object whose `active` is read only by such a filter gets `active` reported as `inert`. No producer in `examples/` or `packages/qa` writes one, so this is a note only.
- **A spec-shaped field-level grant is recorded nowhere** (reported to the seat, not filed here). On `permissions[].fields["inv.region"]` the grant key is never recorded as a carrier. Such a field reads `inert`, and the `fix:` line names no grant site to clean. The rule's docblock and `os explain field-no-consumers` both list "a field-level permission grant" as a carrier. Only the off-spec fixture shape `permissions[].objects.inv.fields.region` (test lines 137, 380 and the RLS block) records one, and `ObjectPermissionSchema` has no `fields` key. Real producer: `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts` (`'showcase_project.budget': {...}`).
- `rule-explanations.ts` (`os explain field-no-consumers`) lists RLS predicates among consumers and does not yet name a field permission's `when`. It is outside this card's declared file surface, so it is left unchanged.
